assessment: This manuscript describes interesting follow-up studies on one peptide hit (from a protein called PCARE) coming out of a proteome-wide screen for peptides that can bind to the EVH1 domain of ENAH, one of the three highly homologous Ena/VASP actin regulators. Surprisingly PCARE binds to ENAH selectively over the other two members of Ena/VASP family, EVL and VASP. The authors provide a nice explanation for how this selectivity is achieved and develop a peptide PCARE-Dual that specifically binds ENAH more tightly, setting out the stage for developing potent and selective inhibitors for ENAH.
